text:
My kids have been in daycare since they were 6 weeks old. I enrolled both of my kids (now 1 and 3) at Kids R Kids because the daycare they were going to had closed. I never found the staff at Kids R Kids to be very friendly, or nurturing towards my kids. Also, the teachers were unable to tell my children 'No'. I am all for 'redirection' learning, but if my child is drawing on walls, I feel that they need to be told that is isn't okay to do that, and tell them 'No'. My kids only went to Kids R Kids for 4 months, during these 4 months my kids became pretty wild. They stopped listening, everything was a fight, we were late everyday - and yes I know, they are 1 and 3, but it was absolute complete chaos! It was outside of the norm of chaos. Kid R Kids has the Watch me Grow system, so I was able to watch my child during the day. Every day they have their learning activities and all the children will sit in a group on the carpet, instead of my child participating I would see my child be redirected to the classroom table practically every day, because they wouldn't just tell her to stop acting up, sit down and listen. Instead they would redirect her to the classroom table with a book (of course she is unable to read by herself because she is 3). So she wasn't able to participate in the learning activities. 

As we are working parents, this daycare center just wasn't working for us. So I pulled them out and moved them to another daycare center. I have waited a of couple months to write this review, but in the last two months my kids are doing so much better, they have respect for others again, they are listening, we are back to the normal chaos, and we are never late anymore. After the first 3 weeks my 3 year old was at their new daycare, she even said to me 'Mommy they don't sit me down to read books by myself anymore' - SERIOUSLY I could not even believe that she said that to me! It breaks my heart the way they are doing business at this daycare center. Kids R Kids is a place where they are just running a business, I don't feel that they actually give individual nurturing attention to the kids that are there. 

A few additional things that I didn't like... 
1. About 90% of the time I walked in to pick up my kids the reception people would never make eye contact. 
2. They always forgot I had two kids, and they could never remember who my kids were when I asked them questions. I'm sorry, when I am paying you $400 a week, I feel that you should at least know who my kids are. 
3. They feed the kids a lot of junk food in the afternoon. I buy candy and cookies, but every day they would have cookies, brownies, pop tarts... just not the healthiest place.  
4. It also didn't seem the teachers in my kids classrooms could think for themselves, the front staff seemed to make all the calls, which I did not like because they weren't the ones actually in the classroom every day with my child. An example, one day I dropped my 3 year old off, she said she didn't feel good. She didn't have a fever and didn't have any symptoms.  I asked her teacher to call me if she didn't eat her morning snack or her lunch, and I would come pick her up before nap time. Well when the time came for her lunch and they didn't call me I felt everything was just fine. Well then front desk called me at 3pm and let me know she hadn't eaten all day. It took them 3 hours to call me. I was so infuriated! Complete lack of communication because the teacher was unable to call me herself, and 
5. My kids got Hand, Foot and Mouth... I know this can go through all daycares, but... it is weird that I was warned about it from a friend before my kids attended Kids R Kids. 

I do not recommend this daycare to anyone. I went and checked out a pre-school for my 3 year old and they were more personable within the 20 minutes I was there taking a tour than Kids R Kids ever was in the 4 months my kids attended. In 4 months we just had way many problems.

text:
I was on vacation in Santa Barbara when the check engine light went on.  I take the car in and the service rep is very nice and personable, but he keeps using different words and phrases than I do and so I feel like communication isn't occurring well.  For example, I say "the car didn't accelerate correctly at low speeds, but accelerated normally once it was going about 15-20 miles per hour."  He repeats back "Loss of power"...which I would interpret as the lights going out, or maybe as the car just not accelerating well at any speed.  In addition to the communication issues, when he gave me the paper record that I dropped my car off and they were inspecting it, the first item listed was "brakes", when we hadn't discussed brakes or braking at all.

Then, I had parked the car right inside the service area and he drove it about 20 feet forward, and when he gets out he makes a big deal about it being jerky/bouncy, when I hadn't noticed anything like that.

I dropped it off in the afternoon, so the next day I get tired of waiting for their call and give them a call about noon because I figured they could have managed to check the code by then.  I find out that the code was due to a sensor glitch and they drove the car and haven't had any more problems with that...but that I have a broken motor mount and that's why it vibrates so much.  I tell them to fix it and I'll pick it up the next day.

The next day I get tired of waiting in the late afternoon and give them a call, finding out they're almost done and I can head over.  When I start driving the car again I can't tell any difference in the way it drives from before I dropped it off.

So far that's not very different from experiences I've had with other car service departments, but as part of the routine inspection they reported all four of my practically new tires as having 5/32nds tread left...then I drove the car 200 miles and had the tires re-checked at an America's Tires as being 8/32nds.  Checking remaining tire tread is a trivial operation, so why the significant difference?  Did Santa Barbara Honda fail at checking the tires, did they give me the wrong inspection sheet, or were they trying to prepare me for buying tires sooner than I needed to just in case they might get that sale?  Now I wonder if maybe I didn't need to spend the extra hundreds of dollars on the motor mount.

text:
The Raven (this pertains to the bar only)
The good:  The raven is a quaint hotel/restaurant/bar that has been an LGBT/New Hope institution for decades.  The two bar areas are not without their charms.  The front main bar looks like a traditional tavern and the back bar is a piano bar that boasts a very talented pianist.  The crowd at the Raven on a typical Saturday night is a pretty good mix of people of different ages, races and genders (including non-binary) though most patrons are middle aged white guys such as myself.  There is a room that is a dance floor and a back patio area that is used by smokers.

The bad: It is hard to find an ideal, comfortable spot at the Raven.  You can sit comfortably in the Siberia of the booth section, but if you do, you're very much in the hinterlands.  The main bar is long and narrow.  You can sit on one of the overly wide, un-cushioned hard bar stools (if you can get one), or stand against the wall and have every passerby knock into you.  The back piano bar often gets very crowded.  The décor of this room could be considered either "fun Gothic" or straight-up cheesy.  The bartenders are generally efficient, but their attitude ranges from neutral to surly.  The on-tap beer selection is four of the worst beers available (the best of which is Yuengling, which means a portion of your bar tab goes to support Donald Trump).  The very worst aspect of The Raven bar is that they serve their draft beer in plastic cups.  Drinking beer from plastic was OK when I was a teenager sneaking drinks at a kegger, but as a paying adult out on a Saturday night, it's just gross.

The bottom line:  If you live in the immediate New Hope area, I can see why this would be your regular night out spot, as there are few, if any, other gay bars near-by.  I could also recommend the Raven as a cool place to visit just to see what it is all about.  Personally, given my geographic location, I'd rather drive the 45 minutes to Philadelphia, and pay for parking, than to travel the half-hour to New Hope for this mediocre bar.

text:
We've heard from a few people that around this area that this place was good.  Since we happened to be in the small town of Souderton we decided to stop in for lunch.  We made a reservation (through Resy), since I hate waiting.  Surprisingly the spots filled pretty quickly, from when my wife checked them to a half an hour later they were nearly booked a few hours out.  That's good for them!

I was surprised to see a smoker in the back of the restaurant with someone putting full racks of ribs on it.  It's definitely a legit smoker, they have the wood stacked nearby and the ribs from where I was standing looked to be St. Louis style ribs.  

The restaurant is nice inside.  It's clean, well laid out and has a good atmosphere.  We got a table on the patio which is fully enclosed and heated.  Due to covid, there were a lot of tables they weren't able to use, so we couldn't grab a seat by the bar (which I prefer).  

The staff were all very friendly and did a great job.  They definitely work as a team which makes our experience better.  

I grabbed a Yards in a can, but they do have a pretty impressive drink list.  This location is part of Boardroom Spirits so all of the alcohol was from BR.  

We came for the pizza, but their menu was more than just that.  I'm not quite sure how to categorize it...it's not a pizza place, it's not a bbq place, it's not a burger place or a salad place; but they offer all of that.

We ordered the Pulled Pork Nachos and the Detroit Style Pepperoni pizza.  The nachos were okay, they honestly would've been better without the pork.  The pork wasn't bad, it just didn't have flavor.  If something is called "smoked", I want to taste smoke and with their offset smoker setup they can definitely bring some flavor.  The cheese on the nachos was good as was the seasoning they put on their chips.  The toppings aside from the pork were good too.  I probably wouldn't order again if I returned.  

The pizza came out and looked great.  I have high expectations for what people call Detroit style...I'm from Detroit and have been eating this stuff before the "foodie" community was even born.  It looked good upon arrival, the cheese was crusted around the edge, the pepperoni had crisped up, the sauce was on top and there was grated parmesan (although more than I would usually expect.  And finally, there was a chiffonade of basil...something I wasn't excited about as I find it can be pretty over powering and if bruised during prep it's way too over powering. 

Took a bite and I was intrigued, the dough was crips along the outside but pillowy soft in the crumb.  The sauce was perfect, a little sweet but not much and it was room temp, not cold, not hot...perfect!  But then the basil, it was delicate, not over powering as I expected and the flavor of it is exactly what a pizza like this needs to cut through the richness of it.  

The pizza is small, only four pieces so if you're hungry or feeding a group get a few.  It's $14 which when you think about it, if you split it, you spent $7 on a very good lunch.  Plus the smaller size means there's less to take home.  

Overall I would definitely return to Northbound.  I want to try some of their cocktails, I want to try some of the other pizzas and some of their ribs.  I'm hoping the nachos were a one off.  But even if everything else on the menu was as underwhelming as the nachos...the pizza makes it worth the visit.
llama_agg_reasoning: The review text expresses overall satisfaction with the restaurant, highlighting the friendly staff, nice atmosphere, and delicious Detroit Style Pepperoni pizza. Although the models are not in complete agreement, BERT's prediction of 4 stars with a relatively high confidence is supported by the reviewer's positive comments and intention to return, outweighing the disagreement from the other models which predicted 3 stars.
